# Spring Boot Web Application using Class Data Sharing (CDS)

Class Data Sharing (CDS) is a Java HotSpot VM feature that improves startup
time and memory footprint by storing preprocessed class metadata in a shared
archive. At startup, the JVM can map that archive instead of reading, parsing,
and recreating the same metadata from class files every time. Because the
archive is memory-mapped, multiple JVM processes on the same machine can also
share parts of the archived metadata.

The default CDS archive covers JDK classes. Application Class-Data Sharing
(AppCDS) extends the same idea to application and dependency classes by
creating an application-specific archive. CDS and AppCDS do not mean the
application has already run, and they do not turn the application into a native
executable. Normal Java class initialisation and application behaviour still
happen when the application starts.

This simple application has one endpoint that returns a random quote from its
database.

A useful way to compare CDS with Project Leyden is to look at the work the JVM
normally performs during startup:

```text
class file on disk
  -> read and parsed
  -> metadata created
  -> class loaded
  -> class linked
  -> class initialized
  -> methods interpreted or JIT compiled
```

CDS focuses on the earlier class-file and metadata work. Project Leyden’s AOT
cache builds on this foundation, but it is not just AppCDS with a new name. The
Leyden AOT cache can preserve later class-processing work too, especially class
loading and linking, so classes can be available in a loaded and linked state
when the JVM starts. This runbook is about CDS, while the separate
[Project Leyden AOT cache example](../leyden-aot-cache-spring-boot/README.md)
covers that newer workflow.

CDS and Leyden are not mutually exclusive at every layer. For example, a
custom runtime image can include a runtime CDS archive created by
`jlink --generate-cds-archive`, and an application can still use a Leyden AOT
cache for its application startup path. The boundary to keep clear is the
application-level workflow: AppCDS and the Leyden AOT cache both target
application startup, but Leyden has the broader scope. Treat them as separate
application-level workflows unless you have verified the exact JDK behaviour
and command-line combination you plan to use.

This runbook separates three related ideas that are easy to blur together:

- **JLink** builds a smaller Java runtime image that contains only the Java
  modules needed by the application.
- **CDS in the runtime image** adds a JVM archive for the classes in that
  custom runtime. This archive is created by `jlink --generate-cds-archive`.
- **Application CDS** creates a separate archive (`app.jsa`) for application
  and dependency class metadata and reuses it on later launches.

The goal is not to prove a universal performance number. The commands below
make each optimisation visible, then compare the startup output from the same
application running on the slim JRE, the CDS-enabled JRE, and the CDS-enabled
JRE plus Application CDS.

**Resources**

- [Java Virtual Machine Guide - 4 Class Data Sharing](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/vm/class-data-sharing.html)
- [CDS with Spring Framework 6.1](https://spring.io/blog/2023/12/04/cds-with-spring-framework-6-1)
- [Spring Framework - CDS](https://docs.spring.io/spring-framework/reference/integration/cds.html)

## Prerequisites

- [Oracle Java 25](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/#java25)

- `jar`, `jdeps` and `jlink`, included with a full JDK installation.

- `curl`, `jq`, `tree`, and `hey`

## Build the application

1. Build the application

   ```shell
   ./mvnw clean verify
   ```

   (*Optional*) Verify that the application was created and the dependencies
   where copied.

   ```shell
   tree -L 1 -P '*.jar' --prune './target/'
   ```

   Spring Boot creates one Fat JAR containing everything in it.

   ```
   ./target/
   └── jlink-cds-image-spring-boot-1.0.0.jar

   1 directory, 1 file
   ```

2. (*Optional*) Run the application

   The application is started in the background for convenience, otherwise the
   subsequent commands need to be executed in another terminal.

   ```shell
   java -jar './target/jlink-cds-image-spring-boot-1.0.0.jar' > './target/output.txt' 2>&1 &
   echo $! > './target/application.pid'
   ```

   Wait for the application to start.

   ```shell
   while [ "$(curl --silent --output /dev/null --write-out '%{http_code}' 'http://localhost:8080/quote/random')" -ne '200' ]
   do
     echo 'Waiting for the application to start'
     sleep 1
   done
   ```

   Fetch a random quote.

   ```shell
   curl --silent 'http://localhost:8080/quote/random' | jq
   ```

   The response should be similar to the following.

   ```json
   {
     "author": "Neil Armstrong",
     "id": 135,
     "quote": "That’s one small step for a man, a giant leap for mankind."
   }
   ```

   Stop the application.

   ```shell
   kill "$(cat './target/application.pid')"
   ```

## Custom JRE

This section continues on the previous section,
[Build the application](#build-the-application), as it takes the JAR file
created there as input to this section.

A JLink image is not a container image. It is a custom Java runtime directory
that can later be copied into a container image. The important part here is the
module list: leave out a required module and the application may start failing
at runtime.

1. (*Optional*) Print the `jdeps` version (which will match that of the JDK).

   ```shell
   jdeps --version
   ```

   The current Java version

   ```
   25.0.4.1
   ```

2. Determine the modules required by our application.

   The
   [`jdeps`](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/docs/specs/man/jdeps.html)
   command can help us with that.

   ```shell
   jdeps \
     --multi-release 25 \
     --ignore-missing-deps \
     --print-module-deps \
     './target/jlink-cds-image-spring-boot-1.0.0.jar'
   ```

   Unfortunately, this will only print `java.base,java.management`, which is
   incorrect.

   ```
   java.base,java.management
   ```

   This result is misleading because the artefact is a repackaged Spring Boot
   executable JAR. The application classes are placed under `BOOT-INF/classes`,
   dependencies are stored as nested JARs under `BOOT-INF/lib`, and the Spring
   Boot launcher builds the runtime classpath when the JAR starts. That layout
   is convenient for `java -jar`, but it is not the normal flat classpath layout
   that static analysis tools such as `jdeps` expect when they inspect the outer
   JAR.

   (*Optional*) Inspect the executable Spring Boot JAR layout.

   ```shell
   jar --list \
     --file './target/jlink-cds-image-spring-boot-1.0.0.jar' |
     grep -E '^(BOOT-INF/classes|BOOT-INF/lib)' |
     head -40
   ```

   The listing shows the application classes and nested dependency JARs inside
   the Spring Boot executable JAR.

   ```
   BOOT-INF/classes/
   BOOT-INF/classes/db/
   BOOT-INF/classes/db/migration/
   BOOT-INF/classes/demo/
   BOOT-INF/classes/demo/quote/
   BOOT-INF/classes/application.yml
   BOOT-INF/classes/db/migration/V1__create_database.sql
   BOOT-INF/classes/banner.txt
   BOOT-INF/classes/demo/Main.class
   BOOT-INF/classes/demo/quote/Quote.class
   BOOT-INF/classes/demo/quote/QuoteController.class
   BOOT-INF/classes/demo/quote/QuoteService.class
   BOOT-INF/classes/demo/quote/QuoteRepository.class
   BOOT-INF/lib/
   BOOT-INF/lib/spring-boot-jackson-4.1.1.jar
   BOOT-INF/lib/jackson-databind-3.1.5.jar
   BOOT-INF/lib/jackson-annotations-2.21.jar
   BOOT-INF/lib/jackson-core-3.1.5.jar
   BOOT-INF/lib/tomcat-embed-core-11.0.24.jar
   BOOT-INF/lib/tomcat-embed-el-11.0.24.jar
   BOOT-INF/lib/tomcat-embed-websocket-11.0.24.jar
   BOOT-INF/lib/spring-boot-tomcat-4.1.1.jar
   BOOT-INF/lib/spring-boot-http-converter-4.1.1.jar
   BOOT-INF/lib/spring-boot-4.1.1.jar
   BOOT-INF/lib/spring-context-7.0.9.jar
   BOOT-INF/lib/spring-web-7.0.9.jar
   BOOT-INF/lib/spring-beans-7.0.9.jar
   BOOT-INF/lib/micrometer-observation-1.17.1.jar
   BOOT-INF/lib/micrometer-commons-1.17.1.jar
   BOOT-INF/lib/spring-boot-webmvc-4.1.1.jar
   BOOT-INF/lib/spring-boot-servlet-4.1.1.jar
   BOOT-INF/lib/spring-webmvc-7.0.9.jar
   BOOT-INF/lib/spring-aop-7.0.9.jar
   BOOT-INF/lib/spring-expression-7.0.9.jar
   BOOT-INF/lib/h2-2.4.240.jar
   BOOT-INF/lib/logback-classic-1.5.38.jar
   BOOT-INF/lib/logback-core-1.5.38.jar
   BOOT-INF/lib/log4j-to-slf4j-2.25.5.jar
   BOOT-INF/lib/log4j-api-2.25.5.jar
   BOOT-INF/lib/jul-to-slf4j-2.0.18.jar
   ```

   To give `jdeps` a dependency view closer to the application’s runtime
   classpath, provide the dependencies explicitly with the `--class-path`
   option. We can obtain the list of dependencies using Maven’s
   `dependency:build-classpath` goal, and save the list of dependencies to file,
   as shown next.

   ```shell
   ./mvnw \
     dependency:build-classpath \
     -Dmdep.outputFile='./target/classpath.txt'
   ```

   (*Optional*) Verify that the class path is saved to file.

   ```shell
   tree --dirsfirst --sort=name -L 1 --prune -P 'classpath.txt' './target'
   ```

   The file containing the runtime classpath

   ```
   ./target
   └── classpath.txt

   1 directory, 1 file
   ```

   Use this file to provide the class path to `jdeps`.

   ```shell
   jdeps \
     --class-path "$(cat './target/classpath.txt')" \
     --multi-release 25 \
     --ignore-missing-deps \
     --print-module-deps \
     './target/jlink-cds-image-spring-boot-1.0.0.jar'
   ```

   This time we will get a lot of more dependencies.

   ```
   java.base,java.compiler,java.desktop,java.instrument,java.management,java.naming,java.net.http,java.prefs,java.rmi,java.scripting,java.security.jgss,java.sql,jdk.jfr,jdk.unsupported
   ```

   Luckily, our application does not need all these dependencies, and we can
   trim this to just.

   ```
   java.base,java.compiler,java.desktop,java.instrument,java.management,java.naming,java.sql,java.security.jgss
   ```

   The `java.compiler` module is required because Spring Data’s AOT repository
   processor uses `javax.lang.model.SourceVersion` at runtime.

   If you are using an older update of Java 21, please note that there is a
   [bug](https://bugs.openjdk.org/browse/JDK-8330005), which does not load the
   random number service provide and fails with the following example. In such a
   case, the time being the `jdk.random` module needs to be added to the list of
   added modules as a workaround.

   ```
   java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: No implementation of the random number generator algorithm "L32X64MixRandom" is available
     at java.base/java.util.random.RandomGeneratorFactory.findProvider(Unknown Source) ~[na:na]
     at java.base/java.util.random.RandomGeneratorFactory.of(Unknown Source) ~[na:na]
     at java.base/java.util.random.RandomGenerator.of(Unknown Source) ~[na:na]
     at java.base/java.util.random.RandomGenerator.getDefault(Unknown Source) ~[na:na]
   ...
   ```

3. (*Optional*) Print the `jlink` version (which will match that of the JDK).

   ```shell
   jlink --version
   ```

   The current Java version

   ```
   25.0.4.1
   ```

4. Create a custom Java runtime (JRE) image using the modules listed in a prior
   step.

   ```shell
   rm -rf './target/slim-jre'
   jlink \
     --output './target/slim-jre' \
     --no-header-files \
     --no-man-pages \
     --add-modules java.base,java.compiler,java.desktop,java.instrument,java.management,java.naming,java.sql,java.security.jgss \
     --strip-debug \
     --compress=zip-9
   ```

   (*Optional*) Measure the size of the custom Java runtime (JRE) image

   ```shell
   du -sh './target/slim-jre'
   ```

   This custom Java runtime (JRE) takes only about `59M`.

   ```
   59M	./target/slim-jre
   ```

   This image contains only the Java modules that are required by this
   application. Different applications may require different modules.

   (*Optional*) List the extracted modules.

   ```shell
   './target/slim-jre/bin/java' --list-modules
   ```

   These are the modules included in our custom image.

   ```
   java.base@25.0.4.1
   java.compiler@25.0.4.1
   java.datatransfer@25.0.4.1
   java.desktop@25.0.4.1
   java.instrument@25.0.4.1
   java.logging@25.0.4.1
   java.management@25.0.4.1
   java.naming@25.0.4.1
   java.prefs@25.0.4.1
   java.security.jgss@25.0.4.1
   java.security.sasl@25.0.4.1
   java.sql@25.0.4.1
   java.transaction.xa@25.0.4.1
   java.xml@25.0.4.1
   ```

   (*Optional*) List the custom Java runtime (JRE) image directory structure.

   ```shell
   tree --dirsfirst --sort=name -L 1 './target/slim-jre'
   ```

   The results are limited to the top level for brevity.

   ```
   ./target/slim-jre
   ├── bin
   ├── conf
   ├── legal
   ├── lib
   └── release

   5 directories, 1 file
   ```

5. Run the application using the custom Java runtime (JRE) image

   The application is started in the background for convenience, otherwise the
   subsequent commands need to be executed in another terminal.

   ```shell
   './target/slim-jre/bin/java' \
     -jar './target/jlink-cds-image-spring-boot-1.0.0.jar' > './target/output.txt' 2>&1 &
   echo $! > './target/application.pid'
   ```

   Wait for the application to start.

   ```shell
   while [ "$(curl --silent --output /dev/null --write-out '%{http_code}' 'http://localhost:8080/quote/random')" -ne '200' ]
   do
     echo 'Waiting for the application to start'
     sleep 1
   done
   ```

   Fetch a random quote.

   ```shell
   curl --silent 'http://localhost:8080/quote/random' | jq
   ```

   The response should be similar to the following.

   ```json
   {
     "author": "Socrates",
     "id": 146,
     "quote": "I cannot teach anybody anything. I can only make them think."
   }
   ```

   Read the time taken for the application to start.

   ```shell
   grep 'Started Main in' './target/output.txt'
   ```

   Time taken for the application to start

   ```
   2077-04-27T11:34:56.789Z  INFO 123456 --- [           main] demo.Main                                : Started Main in 2.958 seconds (process running for 3.357)
   ```

   Stress test the application with 10 thousand requests.

   ```shell

   ```

## Custom CDS JRE

This section continues on the previous section,
[Build the application](#build-the-application), as it takes the JAR file
created there as input to this section.

This image uses the same module list as the slim JRE, but asks JLink to generate
the runtime CDS archive while building the image. The result is usually larger
on disk because the image now includes preprocessed class metadata for the
runtime modules.

1. Create a custom **CDS** Java runtime (JRE) image using the modules listed in
   a prior step.

   ```shell
   rm -rf './target/cds-jre'
   jlink \
     --output './target/cds-jre' \
     --generate-cds-archive \
     --no-header-files \
     --no-man-pages \
     --add-modules java.base,java.compiler,java.desktop,java.instrument,java.management,java.naming,java.sql,java.security.jgss \
     --strip-debug \
     --compress=zip-9
   ```

   (*Optional*) Measure the size of the custom Java runtime (JRE) image

   ```shell
   du -sh './target/cds-jre'
   ```

   This custom **CDS** Java runtime (JRE) takes about `87M`, which is larger
   than the `59M` slim custom image with the same modules.

   ```
   87M	./target/cds-jre
   ```

   (*Optional*) Show the generated runtime CDS archive.

   ```shell
   tree -L 2 -P 'classes.jsa' --prune './target/cds-jre/lib'
   ```

   The `classes.jsa` file is the runtime CDS archive generated by JLink.

   ```
   ./target/cds-jre/lib
   └── server
       └── classes.jsa

   2 directories, 1 file
   ```

   (*Optional*) List the extracted modules.

   ```shell
   './target/cds-jre/bin/java' --list-modules
   ```

   These are the modules included in our custom **CDS** image.

   ```
   java.base@25.0.4.1
   java.compiler@25.0.4.1
   java.datatransfer@25.0.4.1
   java.desktop@25.0.4.1
   java.instrument@25.0.4.1
   java.logging@25.0.4.1
   java.management@25.0.4.1
   java.naming@25.0.4.1
   java.prefs@25.0.4.1
   java.security.jgss@25.0.4.1
   java.security.sasl@25.0.4.1
   java.sql@25.0.4.1
   java.transaction.xa@25.0.4.1
   java.xml@25.0.4.1
   ```

   (*Optional*) List the custom **CDS** Java runtime (JRE) image directory
   structure.

   ```shell
   tree -L 1 './target/cds-jre'
   ```

   The results are limited to the top level for brevity.

   ```
   ./target/cds-jre
   ├── bin
   ├── conf
   ├── legal
   ├── lib
   └── release

   5 directories, 1 file
   ```

2. Run the application using the custom **CDS** Java runtime (JRE) image

   The application is started in the background for convenience, otherwise the
   subsequent commands need to be executed in another terminal.

   ```shell
   './target/cds-jre/bin/java' \
     '-Xlog:cds*=info' \
     -jar './target/jlink-cds-image-spring-boot-1.0.0.jar' > './target/output.txt' 2>&1 &
   echo $! > './target/application.pid'
   ```

   Wait for the application to start.

   ```shell
   while [ "$(curl --silent --output /dev/null --write-out '%{http_code}' 'http://localhost:8080/quote/random')" -ne '200' ]
   do
     echo 'Waiting for the application to start'
     sleep 1
   done
   ```

   Fetch a random quote.

   ```shell
   curl --silent 'http://localhost:8080/quote/random' | jq
   ```

   The response should be similar to the following.

   ```json
   {
     "author": "Benjamin Franklin",
     "id": 39,
     "quote": "To succeed, jump as quickly at opportunities as you do at conclusions."
   }
   ```

   Confirm that the JVM used the runtime CDS archive from the custom image.


   The `trying to map` and `Opened shared archive file` lines identify the

   Read the time taken for the application to start.

## Custom CDS JRE + Application CDS

This section continues on the previous sections,
[Build the application](#build-the-application) and
[Custom CDS JRE](#custom-cds-jre), as it takes the JAR file created there as
input to this section.

Runtime CDS covers classes from the custom runtime image. Application CDS adds
a second archive for classes loaded from this Spring Boot application and its
dependencies. Spring’s `spring.context.exit=onRefresh` option lets us warm the
application context, write the archive, and exit without leaving the HTTP
server running.

If you later use the Leyden AOT cache example with a custom runtime, keep the
runtime CDS archive and application cache concerns separate. Runtime CDS belongs
to the JLink-built runtime image. AppCDS and Leyden's AOT cache are
application-level startup workflows, so this section uses AppCDS by itself
rather than stacking it with Leyden.

1. Create the application **CDS**.

   ```shell
   rm -f './target/app.jsa' './target/application.pid'
   './target/cds-jre/bin/java' \
     -Dspring.context.exit=onRefresh \
     -XX:+AutoCreateSharedArchive \
     -XX:SharedArchiveFile='./target/app.jsa' \
     -jar './target/jlink-cds-image-spring-boot-1.0.0.jar' > './target/output.txt' 2>&1
   ```

   The application will automatically shut down once it starts, as instructed by
   the `-Dspring.context.exit=onRefresh` option.

   ```shell
   tree -L 1 --prune './target'
   ```

   The `app.jsa` contains our application CDS archive and can be used in
   subsequent runs

   ```
   ./target
   ├── app.jsa
   ├── classpath.txt
   ├── jlink-cds-image-spring-boot-1.0.0.jar
   ├── jlink-cds-image-spring-boot-1.0.0.jar.original
   └── output.txt

   1 directory, 5 files
   ```

   (*Optional*) Confirm that the archive was written and inspect its size.

   ```shell
   ls -lh './target/app.jsa'
   ```

   Application CDS is a separate archive from the JLink runtime image.

   ```
   -rw-r--r--. 1 opc opc 75M Apr 27 12:34 ./target/app.jsa
   ```

2. Run the application using the custom CDS Java runtime (JRE) image and the
   application CDS

   The application is started in the background for convenience, otherwise the
   subsequent commands need to be executed in another terminal.

   ```shell
   './target/cds-jre/bin/java' \
     '-Xlog:cds*=info' \
     -XX:SharedArchiveFile='./target/app.jsa' \
     -jar './target/jlink-cds-image-spring-boot-1.0.0.jar' > './target/output.txt' 2>&1 &
   echo $! > './target/application.pid'
   ```

   Wait for the application to start.

   ```shell
   while [ "$(curl --silent --output /dev/null --write-out '%{http_code}' 'http://localhost:8080/quote/random')" -ne '200' ]
   do
     echo 'Waiting for the application to start'
     sleep 1
   done
   ```

   Fetch a random quote.

   ```shell
   curl --silent 'http://localhost:8080/quote/random' | jq
   ```

   The response should be similar to the following.

   ```json
   {
     "author": "Albert Einstein",
     "id": 6,
     "quote": "A person who never made a mistake never tried anything new."
   }
   ```

   Confirm that the JVM used the application CDS archive.

   This run opens two CDS archives. The `classes.jsa` archive comes from the
   custom runtime image and remains the base runtime archive. The `app.jsa`
   archive is the application archive passed through `-XX:SharedArchiveFile`.
   This split is useful because the runtime archive can be reused by every
   application that uses the same custom JRE, while the application archive can
   be rebuilt only when this application or its dependencies change. In a
   container image, that also gives you a stable runtime layer and a more
   application-specific CDS layer.

   ```shell
   grep -E 'trying to map|Opened shared archive file|Mapped static|Mapped dynamic' './target/output.txt' | head
   ```

   The first archive path identifies the runtime `classes.jsa` archive from the
   custom image. The second archive path identifies the application `app.jsa`
   archive passed through `-XX:SharedArchiveFile`. The `Mapped static` lines
   confirm the base archive mapping, while `Mapped dynamic` lines, when shown,
   confirm the application archive mapping.

   ```
   [0.007s][info][cds] trying to map ./target/cds-jre/lib/server/classes.jsa
   [0.007s][info][cds] Opened shared archive file ./target/cds-jre/lib/server/classes.jsa.
   [0.007s][info][cds] trying to map ./target/app.jsa
   [0.008s][info][cds] Opened shared archive file ./target/app.jsa.
   [0.008s][info][cds] Mapped static  region #0 at base 0x0000000009001000 top 0x00000000094a7000 (ReadWrite)
   [0.008s][info][cds] Mapped static  region #1 at base 0x00000000094a7000 top 0x0000000009c7c000 (ReadOnly)
   [0.008s][info][cds] Mapped static  region #2 at base 0x00007f2ec34fb000 top 0x00007f2ec3529000 (Bitmap)
   [0.011s][info][cds] Mapped dynamic region #0 at base 0x0000000009c7c000 top 0x000000000bdb5000 (ReadWrite)
   [0.011s][info][cds] Mapped dynamic region #1 at base 0x000000000bdb5000 top 0x000000000e630000 (ReadOnly)
   [0.011s][info][cds] Mapped dynamic region #2 at base 0x00007f2ea4003000 top 0x00007f2ea40fa000 (Bitmap)
   ```

   Read the time taken for the application to start.

   ```shell
   grep 'Started Main in' './target/output.txt'
   ```

   The time taken for the application to start.

   ```
   2077-04-27T11:35:19.980Z  INFO 123456 --- [           main] demo.Main                                : Started Main in 2.173 seconds (process running for 2.516)
   ```

   Stress test the application with 10 thousand requests.

   ```shell
   hey -n=10000 'http://localhost:8080/quote/random'
   ```

   The stress test results


   Stop the application.

   ```shell
   kill "$(cat './target/application.pid')"
   ```

3. Analyse results

   | Runtime                           | Runtime Size | App CDS Archive |  Startup Time |            Throughput |  Latency (P95) |
   | --------------------------------- | -----------: | --------------: | ------------: | --------------------: | -------------: |
   | Slim JRE                          |        `59M` |               - | `2.958` (sec) | `4512.0613` (req/sec) | `0.0253` (sec) |
   | Custom CDS JRE                    |        `87M` |               - | `3.027` (sec) | `4727.5754` (req/sec) | `0.0243` (sec) |
   | Runtime CDS JRE + Application CDS |        `87M` |           `75M` | `2.173` (sec) | `4162.1313` (req/sec) | `0.0262` (sec) |

   Treat these numbers as local observations from this machine and run, not as
   portable benchmarks. The useful comparison is the direction and magnitude
   across the three configurations.
